technologies with enterprise resource planning or other system software.

tasks: [Core] Fill customer orders by packaging sold items and documentation for direct shipping or by transferring orders to manufacturers or third-party distributors. | [Core] Receive and process payments from customers, using electronic transaction services. | [Core] Create, manage, or automate orders or invoices, using order management or invoicing software. | [Core] Deliver e-mail confirmation of completed transactions and shipment. | [Core] Correspond with online customers via electronic mail, telephone, or other electronic messaging to address questions or complaints about products, policies, or shipping methods. | [Core] Purchase new or used items from online or physical sources for resale via retail or auction Web site. | [Core] Determine and set product prices. | shopping Web sites. | [Core] Compose images of products, using video or still cameras, lighting equipment, props, or photo or video editing software. | [Core] Upload digital media, such as photos, online traffic. | [Core] Create or maintain database of customer accounts. | [Core] Promote products in online communities through weblog or discussion-forum postings, e-mail marketing programs, or online advertising. | [Core] Collaborate with search engine shopping specialists to place marketing content in desired online locations. | [Core] Investigate products or markets to determine areas for opportunity or viability for merchandising specific products, using online or offline sources. | [Core] Maintain inventory of shipping supplies, such as boxes, labels, tape, bubble wrap, loose packing materials, or tape guns. | [Core] Measure and analyze Web site usage data to maximize search engine returns or refine customer interfaces. | [Core] Develop or revise business plans for online business, emphasizing factors such as product line, pricing, inventory, or marketing strategy. | [Core] Disclose merchant information and terms and policies of transactions in online or offline materials. | [Supplemental] Design customer interface of online storefront, using web programming or e-commerce software. | [Supplemental] Select and purchase technical web services, such as web hosting services, online merchant accounts, shopping cart software, payment gateway software, or spyware. | [Supplemental] Transfer digital media, such as music, video, or software, to customers via the Internet. | [Supplemental] Devise, select, or purchase domain name and web address. | [Supplemental] Initiate online auctions through auction hosting sites or auction management software. | encryption, or firewalls. | [Supplemental] Investigate sources, such as auctions, estate sales, liquidators, wholesalers, or trade shows for new items, used items, or collectibles. | [Supplemental] Participate in online forums or conferences to stay abreast of online retailing trends, techniques, or security threats. | [Supplemental] Integrate online retailing strategy with physical or catalogue retailing operations. | [Supplemental] Create or distribute offline promotional material, such as brochures, pamphlets, business cards, stationary, or signage.

management about asset utilization and audit results, and recommend changes in operations and financial activities.

Prepare written reports that estimate property values, outline methods by which the estimations were made, and meet appraisal standards. | [Core] Photograph interiors and exteriors of properties to assist in estimating property value, substantiate findings, and complete appraisal reports. | [Core] Search public records for transactions such as sales, leases, and assessments. | [Core] Obtain county land values and sales information about nearby properties to aid in establishment of property values. | [Core] Maintain familiarity with aspects of local real estate markets. | [Core] Inspect properties, considering factors such as market value, location, and building or replacement costs to determine appraisal value. | [Core] Collect and analyze relevant data to identify real estate market trends. | [Core] Review information about transfers of property to ensure its accuracy, checking basic information on buyers, sellers, and sales prices and making corrections as necessary. | [Core] Analyze trends in sales prices, construction costs, and rents, to assess property values or determine the accuracy of assessments. | [Core] Inspect new construction and major improvements to existing structures to determine values. | [Core] Check building codes and zoning bylaws to determine any effects on the properties being appraised. | [Core] Interview persons familiar with properties and immediate surroundings, such as contractors, home owners, and realtors, to obtain pertinent information. | [Core] Verify legal descriptions of properties by comparing them to county records. | [Core] Evaluate land and neighborhoods where properties are situated, considering locations and trends or impending changes that could influence future values. | [Core] Examine the type and location of nearby services, such as shopping centers, schools, parks, and other neighborhood features, to evaluate their impact on property values. | [Core] Examine income records and operating costs of income properties. | [Core] Estimate building replacement costs, using building valuation manuals and professional cost estimators. | [Core] Draw land diagrams to be used in appraisal reports to support findings. | [Core] Conduct regular reviews of property within jurisdictions to determine changes in property due to construction or demolition. | [Core] Testify in court as to the value of a piece of real estate property. | [Supplemental] Identify the ownership of each piece of taxable property. | [Supplemental] Prepare and maintain current data on each parcel assessed, including maps of boundaries, inventories of land and structures, property characteristics, and any applicable exemptions. | [Supplemental] Establish uniform and equitable systems for assessing all classes and kinds of property. | [Supplemental] Calculate tax bills for properties by multiplying assessed values by jurisdiction tax rates. | [Supplemental] Determine taxability of properties, using methods such as field inspection, structural measurement, calculation, sales analysis, market trend studies, and income and expense analysis. | [Supplemental] Explain assessed values to property owners and defend appealed assessments at public hearings. | [Supplemental] Explain real and personal property taxes to property owners.

tasks: [Core] Interview clients to determine their current income, expenses, insurance coverage, tax status, financial objectives, risk tolerance, or other information needed to develop a financial plan. | [Core] Analyze financial information obtained from clients to determine strategies for meeting clients' financial objectives. | [Core] Answer clients' questions about the purposes and details of financial plans and strategies. | [Core] Review clients' accounts and plans regularly to determine whether life changes, economic changes, environmental concerns, or financial performance indicate a need for plan reassessment. | [Core] Manage client portfolios, keeping client plans up-to-date. | [Core] Recommend to clients strategies in cash management, insurance coverage, investment planning, or other areas to help them achieve their financial goals. | [Core] Recommend financial products, such as stocks, bonds, mutual funds, or insurance. | [Core] Implement financial planning recommendations, or refer clients to someone who can assist them with plan implementation. | [Core] Contact clients periodically to determine any changes in their financial status. | [Core] Prepare or interpret for clients information, such as investment performance reports, financial document summaries, or income projections. | [Core] Explain to clients the personal financial advisor's responsibilities and the types of services to be provided. | [Core] Investigate available investment opportunities to determine compatibility with client financial plans. | [Core] Guide clients in the gathering of information, such as bank account records, income tax returns, life and disability insurance records, pension plans, or wills. | [Core] Monitor financial market trends to ensure that client plans are responsive. | [Core] Recruit and maintain client bases. | [Core] Meet with clients' other advisors, such as attorneys, accountants, trust officers, or investment bankers, to fully understand clients' financial goals and circumstances. | [Core] Devise debt liquidation plans that include payoff priorities and timelines. | [Supplemental] Open accounts for clients, and disburse funds from accounts to creditors as agent for clients. | [Supplemental] Inform clients about tax benefits, government rebates, or other financial benefits of alternative-fuel vehicle purchases or energy-efficient home construction, improvements, or remodeling. | [Supplemental] Recommend environmentally responsible investments, such as cleantech, alternative energy, or conservation technologies, companies, or funds. | [Supplemental] Conduct seminars or workshops on financial planning topics, such as retirement planning, estate planning, or the evaluation of severance packages.

resolve problems with returns. | [Core] Notify taxpayers of any overpayment or underpayment, and either issue a refund or request further payment. | [Core] Maintain records for each case, including taxpayers and assist them in completing tax forms. | [Supplemental] Collect taxes from individuals or businesses according to prescribed laws and regulations. | [Supplemental] Determine appropriate methods of debt settlement, such as offers of compromise, wage garnishment, or seizure and sale of property. | [Supplemental] Check tax forms to verify that names and taxpayer identification numbers are correct, that computations have been performed correctly, or that amounts match those on supporting documentation. | [Supplemental] Examine and analyze tax assets and liabilities to determine resolution of delinquent tax problems. | [Supplemental] Impose payment deadlines on delinquent taxpayers and monitor payments to ensure that deadlines are met. | [Supplemental] Direct service of legal documents, such as subpoenas, warrants, notices of assessment, and garnishments. | [Supplemental] Review filed tax returns to determine whether claimed tax credits and deductions are allowed by law. | [Supplemental] Maintain knowledge of tax code changes, and of accounting procedures and theory to properly evaluate financial information. | [Supplemental] Investigate claims of inability to pay taxes by researching court information for the status of liens, mortgages, or financial statements, or by locating assets through third parties. | [Supplemental] Review selected tax returns to determine the nature and extent of audits to be performed on them. | [Supplemental] Examine accounting systems and records to determine whether accounting methods used were appropriate and in compliance with statutory provisions. | [Supplemental] Participate in informal appeals hearings on contested cases from other agents. | [Supplemental] Prepare briefs and assist in searching and seizing records to prepare charges and documentation for court cases. | [Supplemental] Enter tax return information into computers for processing. | [Supplemental] Secure a taxpayer's agreement to discharge a tax assessment or submit contested determinations to other administrative or judicial conferees for appeals hearings.

tasks: [Core] Assist in determining document management policies to facilitate efficient, legal, and secure access to electronic content. | [Core] Assist in the development of document or content classification taxonomies to facilitate information capture, search, and retrieval. | [Core] Implement electronic document processing, retrieval, and distribution systems in collaboration with other information technology specialists. | [Core] Identify and classify documents or other electronic content according to characteristics such as security level, function, and metadata. | [Core] Develop, document, or maintain standards, best practices, or system usage procedures. | [Core] Assist in the assessment, acquisition, or deployment of new electronic document management systems. | [Core] Administer document and system access rights and revision control to ensure security of system and integrity of master documents. | [Core] Prepare and record changes to official documents and confirm changes with legal and compliance management staff, including enterprise-wide records management staff. | [Core] Write, review, or execute plans for testing new or established document management systems. | [Core] Monitor regulatory activity to maintain compliance with records and document management laws. | [Core] Retrieve electronic assets from repository for distribution to users, collecting and returning to repository, if necessary. | [Core] Keep abreast of developments in document management technologies and techniques by reviewing current literature, talking with colleagues, participating in educational programs, attending meetings or workshops, or participating in professional organizations or conferences. | [Core] Conduct needs assessments to identify document management requirements of departments or end users. | [Core] Develop or configure document management system features, such as user interfaces, access profiles, and document workflow procedures. | [Core] Document technical functions and specifications for new or proposed content management systems. | [Core] Exercise security surveillance over document processing, reproduction, distribution, storage, or archiving. | [Core] Consult with end users regarding problems in accessing electronic content. | [Core] Propose recommendations for improving content management system capabilities. | [Core] Operate data capture technology to import digitized documents into document management system. | [Core] Prepare support documentation and training materials for end users of document management systems. | [Core] Search electronic sources, such as databases or repositories, or manual sources for information. | [Core] Implement scanning or other automated data entry procedures, using imaging devices and document imaging software. | [Supplemental] Analyze, interpret, or disseminate system performance data.

surveys to describe, certify, and assume liability for work performed. | [Core] Write descriptions of property boundary surveys for use in deeds, leases, or other legal documents. | [Core] Verify the accuracy of survey data, including measurements and calculations conducted at survey sites. | [Core] Search legal records, survey records, and land titles to obtain information about property boundaries in areas to be surveyed. | [Core] Record the results of surveys, including the shape, contour, location, elevation, and dimensions of land or land features. | [Core] Prepare, or supervise preparation of, all data, charts, plots, maps, records, and documents related to surveys. | [Core] Compute geodetic measurements and interpret survey data to determine positions, shapes, and elevations of geomorphic and topographic features. | [Core] Calculate heights, depths, relative positions, property lines, and other characteristics of terrain. | [Core] Plan and conduct ground surveys designed to establish baselines, elevations, and other geodetic measurements. | [Core] Establish fixed points for use in making maps, using geodetic and engineering instruments. | [Core] Determine longitudes and latitudes of important features and boundaries in survey areas, using theodolites, transits, levels, and satellite-based global positioning systems (GPS). | [Core] Train assistants and helpers, and direct their work in such activities as performing surveys or drafting maps. | [Core] Coordinate findings with the work of engineering and architectural personnel, clients, and others concerned with projects. | [Core] Analyze survey objectives and specifications to prepare survey proposals or to direct others in survey proposal preparation. | [Core] Testify as an expert witness in court cases on land survey issues, such as property boundaries. | [Core] Adjust surveying instruments to maintain their accuracy. | [Core] Develop criteria for survey methods and procedures. | [Core] Survey bodies of water to determine navigable channels and to secure data for construction of breakwaters, piers, and other marine structures. | [Core] Direct aerial surveys of specified geographical areas. | [Core] Conduct research in surveying and mapping methods, using knowledge of photogrammetric map compilation and electronic data processing. | [Supplemental] Locate and mark sites selected for geophysical prospecting activities, such as efforts to locate petroleum or other mineral products. | [Supplemental] Determine specifications for equipment to be used for aerial photography, as well as altitudes from which to photograph terrain. | [Supplemental] Develop criteria for the design and modification of survey instruments.

transfers. | [Core] Select cleaning materials, tools, or equipment. | [Supplemental] Calibrate or adjust equipment to ensure quality production, using tools such as calipers, micrometers, height tasks: [Core] Identify environmental impacts caused by products, systems, or projects. | [Core] Identify or develop strategies or methods to minimize the environmental impact of industrial production processes. | [Core] Analyze changes designed to improve the environmental performance of complex systems and avoid unintended negative consequences. | [Core] Conduct environmental sustainability assessments, using material flow analysis (MFA) or substance flow analysis (SFA) techniques. | [Core] Identify sustainable alternatives to industrial or waste-management practices. | [Core] Review research literature to maintain knowledge on topics related to industrial ecology, such as physical science, technology, economy, and public policy. | [Core] Redesign linear, or open-loop, systems into cyclical, or closed-loop, systems so that waste products become inputs for new processes, modeling natural ecosystems. | [Core] Prepare technical and research reports, such as environmental impact reports, and communicate the results to individuals in industry, government, or the general public. | [Core] Examine local, regional, or global use and flow of materials or energy in industrial production processes. | [Core] Monitor the environmental impact of development activities, pollution, or land degradation. | [Core] Build and maintain databases of information about energy alternatives, pollutants, natural environments, industrial processes, and other information related to ecological change. | [Core] Perform analyses to determine how human behavior can affect, and be affected by, changes in the environment. | [Core] Recommend methods to protect the environment or minimize environmental damage from industrial production practices. | [Core] Translate the theories of industrial ecology into eco-industrial practices. | [Core] Develop alternative energy investment scenarios to compare economic and environmental costs and benefits. | [Core] Carry out environmental assessments in accordance with applicable standards, regulations, or laws. | [Core] Examine societal issues and their relationship with both technical systems and the environment. | [Core] Plan or conduct field research on topics such as industrial production, industrial ecology, population ecology, and environmental production or sustainability. | [Core] Create complex and dynamic mathematical models of population, community, or ecological systems. | [Core] Evaluate the effectiveness of industrial ecology programs, using statistical analysis and applications. | [Core] Forecast future status or condition of ecosystems, based on changing industrial practices or environmental conditions. | [Core] Review industrial practices, such as the methods and materials used in construction or production, to identify potential liabilities and environmental hazards. | [Core] Apply new or existing research about natural ecosystems to understand economic and industrial systems in the context of the environment. | [Core] Prepare plans to manage renewable resources. | [Core] Identify or compare the component parts or relationships between the parts of industrial, social, and natural systems. | [Core] Plan or conduct studies of the ecological implications of historic or projected changes in industrial processes or development. | [Core] Research sources of pollution to determine environmental impact or to develop methods of pollution abatement or control. | [Core] Perform environmentally extended input-output (EE I-O) analyses. | [Core] Promote use of environmental management systems (EMS) to reduce waste or to improve environmentally sound use of natural resources. | [Core] Investigate the impact of changed land management or land use practices on ecosystems. | [Supplemental] Develop or test protocols to monitor ecosystem components and ecological processes. | [Supplemental] Research environmental effects of land and water use to determine methods of improving environmental conditions or increasing outputs, such as crop yields. | [Supplemental] Provide industrial managers with technical materials on environmental issues, regulatory guidelines, or compliance actions. | [Supplemental] Conduct applied research on the effects of industrial processes on the protection, restoration, inventory, monitoring, or reintroduction of species to the natural environment. | [Supplemental] Conduct scientific protection, mitigation, or restoration projects to prevent resource damage, maintain the integrity of critical habitats, and minimize the impact of human activities. | [Supplemental] Investigate accidents affecting the environment to assess ecological impact. | [Supplemental] Conduct analyses to determine the maximum amount of work that can be accomplished for a given amount of energy in a system, such as industrial production systems and waste treatment systems. | [Supplemental] Investigate the adaptability of various animal and plant species to changed environmental conditions.

tasks: [Core] Collect information and make judgments through observation, interviews, and review of documents. | [Core] Teach or mentor undergraduate and graduate students in anthropology or archeology. | [Core] Write about and present research findings for a variety of specialized and general audiences. | [Core] Plan and direct research to characterize and compare the economic, demographic, health care, social, political, linguistic, and religious institutions of distinct cultural groups, communities, and organizations. | [Core] Create data records for use in describing and analyzing social patterns and processes, using photography, videography, and audio recordings. | [Core] Train others in the application of ethnographic research methods to solve problems in organizational effectiveness, communications, technology development, policy making, and program planning. | [Core] Identify culturally specific beliefs and practices affecting health status and access to services for distinct populations and communities, in collaboration with medical and public health officials. | [Core] Apply traditional ecological knowledge and assessments of culturally distinctive land and resource management institutions to assist in the resolution of conflicts over habitat protection and resource enhancement. | [Core] Lead field training sites and train field staff, students, and volunteers in excavation methods. | [Core] Conduct participatory action research in communities and organizations to assess how work is done and to design work systems, technologies, and environments. | [Core] Develop and test theories concerning the origin and development of past cultures. | [Core] Research, survey, or assess sites of past societies and cultures in search of answers to specific research questions. | [Core] Write grant proposals to obtain funding for research. | [Core] Advise government agencies, private organizations, and communities regarding proposed programs, plans, and policies and their potential impacts on cultural institutions, organizations, and communities. | [Core] Organize public exhibits and displays to promote public awareness of diverse and distinctive cultural traditions. | [Core] Collaborate with economic development planners to decide on the implementation of proposed development policies, plans, and programs based on culturally institutionalized barriers and facilitating circumstances. | [Core] Develop intervention procedures, using techniques such as individual and focus group interviews, consultations, and participant observation of social interaction. | [Core] Enhance the cultural sensitivity of elementary and secondary curricula and classroom interactions in collaboration with educators and teachers. | [Core] Study archival collections of primary historical sources to help explain the origins and development of cultural patterns. | [Core] Formulate general rules that describe and predict the development and behavior of cultures and social institutions. | [Supplemental] Record the exact locations and conditions of artifacts uncovered in diggings or surveys, using drawings and photographs as necessary. | [Supplemental] Assess archeological sites for resource management, development, or conservation purposes and recommend methods for site protection. | [Supplemental] Gather and analyze artifacts and skeletal remains to increase knowledge of ancient cultures. | [Supplemental] Compare findings from one site with archeological data from other sites to find similarities or differences. | [Supplemental] Describe artifacts' physical properties or attributes, such as the materials from which artifacts are made and their size, shape, function, and decoration. | [Supplemental] Collect artifacts made of stone, bone, metal, and other materials, placing them in bags and marking them to show where they were found. | [Supplemental] Study objects and structures recovered by excavation to identify, date, and authenticate them and to interpret their significance. | [Supplemental] Consult site reports, existing artifacts, and topographic maps to identify archeological sites. | [Supplemental] Clean, restore, and preserve artifacts. | [Supplemental] Participate in forensic activities, such as tooth and bone structure identification, in conjunction with police departments and pathologists.

tasks: [Core] Interpret laws, rulings and regulations for individuals and businesses. | [Core] Analyze the probable outcomes of cases, using knowledge of legal precedents. | [Core] Gather evidence to formulate defense or to initiate legal actions by such means as interviewing clients and witnesses to ascertain the facts of a case. | [Core] Represent clients in court or before government agencies. | [Core] Evaluate findings and develop strategies and arguments in preparation for presentation of cases. | [Core] Advise clients concerning business transactions, claim liability, advisability of prosecuting or defending lawsuits, or legal rights and obligations. | [Core] Examine legal data to determine advisability of defending or prosecuting lawsuit. | [Core] Prepare, draft, and review legal documents, such as wills, deeds, patent applications, mortgages, leases, and contracts. | [Core] Study Constitution, statutes, decisions, regulations, and ordinances of quasi-judicial bodies to determine ramifications for cases. | [Core] Negotiate settlements of civil disputes. | [Core] Supervise legal assistants. | [Core] Negotiate contractual agreements. | [Core] Confer with colleagues with specialties in appropriate areas of legal issue to establish and verify bases for legal proceedings. | [Core] Search for and examine public and other legal records to write opinions or establish ownership. | [Core] Perform administrative and management functions related to the practice of law. | [Supplemental] Present and summarize cases to judges and juries. | [Supplemental] Select jurors, argue motions, meet with judges, and question witnesses during the course of a trial. | [Supplemental] Present evidence to defend clients or prosecute defendants in criminal or civil litigation. | [Supplemental] Probate wills and represent and advise executors and administrators of estates. | [Supplemental] Prepare legal briefs and opinions, and file appeals in state and federal courts of appeal. | [Supplemental] Act as agent, trustee, guardian, or executor for businesses or individuals. | [Supplemental] Help develop federal and state programs, draft and interpret laws and legislation, and establish enforcement procedures.

tasks: [Core] Use materials such as pens and ink, watercolors, charcoal, oil, or computer software to create artwork. | [Core] Integrate and develop visual elements, such as line, space, mass, color, and perspective, to produce desired effects, such as the illustration of ideas, emotions, or moods. | [Core] Confer with clients, editors, writers, art directors, and other interested parties regarding the nature and content of artwork to be produced. | [Core] Maintain portfolios of artistic work to demonstrate styles, interests, and abilities. | [Core] Market artwork through brochures, mailings, or Web sites. | [Core] Study different techniques to learn how to apply them to artistic endeavors. | [Core] Monitor events, trends, and other circumstances, research specific subject areas, attend art exhibitions, and read art publications to develop ideas and keep current on art world activities. | [Core] Photograph objects, places, or scenes for reference material. | [Supplemental] Model substances such as clay or wax, using fingers and small hand tools to form objects. | [Supplemental] Create sculptures, statues, and other three-dimensional artwork by using abrasives and tools to shape, carve, and fabricate materials such as clay, stone, wood, or metal. | [Supplemental] Set up exhibitions of artwork for display or sale. | [Supplemental] Render drawings, illustrations, and sketches of buildings, manufactured products, or models, working from sketches, blueprints, memory, models, or reference materials. | [Supplemental] Shade and fill in sketch outlines and backgrounds, using a variety of media such as water colors, markers, and transparent washes, labeling designated colors when necessary. | [Supplemental] Frame and mat artwork for display or sale. | [Supplemental] Submit artwork to shows or galleries. | [Supplemental] Submit preliminary or finished artwork or project plans to clients for approval, incorporating changes as necessary. | [Supplemental] Collaborate with engineers, mechanics, and other technical experts as necessary to build and install creations. | [Supplemental] Cut, bend, laminate, arrange, and fasten individual or mixed raw and manufactured materials and products to form works of art. | [Supplemental] Provide entertainment at special events by performing activities such as drawing cartoons. | [Supplemental] Develop project budgets for approval, estimating time lines and material costs. | [Supplemental] Create and prepare sketches and model drawings of cartoon characters, providing details from memory, live models, manufactured products, or reference materials. | [Supplemental] Create finished art work as decoration, or to elucidate or substitute for spoken or written messages. | [Supplemental] Create sketches, profiles, or likenesses of posed subjects or photographs, using any combination of freehand drawing, mechanical assembly kits, and computer imaging. | [Supplemental] Trace drawings onto clear acetate for painting or coloring, or trace them with ink to make final copies. | [Supplemental] Apply solvents and cleaning agents to clean surfaces of paintings, and to remove accretions, discolorations, and deteriorated varnish. | [Supplemental] Collaborate with writers who create ideas, stories, or captions that are combined with artists' work. | [Supplemental] Brush or spray protective or decorative finishes on completed background panels, informational legends, exhibit accessories, or finished paintings. | [Supplemental] Teach artistic techniques to children or adults.

tasks: [Core] Develop set designs, based on evaluation of scripts, budgets, research information, and available locations. | [Core] Prepare rough drafts and scale working drawings of sets, including floor plans, scenery, and properties to be constructed. | [Core] Prepare preliminary renderings of proposed exhibits, including detailed construction, layout, and material specifications, and diagrams relating to aspects such as special effects or lighting. | [Core] Read scripts to determine location, set, and design requirements. | [Core] Submit plans for approval, and adapt plans to serve intended purposes, or to conform to budget or fabrication restrictions. | [Core] Attend rehearsals and production meetings to obtain and share information related to sets. | [Core] Confer with clients and staff to gather information about exhibit space, proposed themes and content, timelines, budgets, materials, or promotion requirements. | [Core] Research architectural and stylistic elements appropriate to the time period to be depicted, consulting experts for information, as necessary. | [Core] Observe sets during rehearsals in order to ensure that set elements do not interfere with performance aspects such as cast movement and camera angles. | [Core] Collaborate with those in charge of lighting and sound so that those production aspects can be coordinated with set designs or exhibit layouts. | [Core] Select set props, such as furniture, pictures, lamps, and rugs. | [Core] Design and build scale models of set designs, or miniature sets used in filming backgrounds or special effects. | [Core] Examine objects to be included in exhibits to plan where and how to display them. | [Core] Assign staff to complete design ideas and prepare sketches, illustrations, and detailed drawings of sets, or graphics and animation. | [Core] Inspect installed exhibits for conformance to specifications and satisfactory operation of special-effects components. | [Core] Estimate set- or exhibit-related costs, including materials, construction, and rental of props or locations. | [Core] Plan for location-specific issues, such as space limitations, traffic flow patterns, and safety concerns. | [Core] Acquire, or arrange for acquisition of, specimens or graphics required to complete exhibits. | [Core] Design and produce displays and materials that can be used to decorate windows, interior displays, or event locations, such as streets and fairgrounds. | [Supplemental] Direct and coordinate construction, erection, or decoration activities to ensure that sets or exhibits meet design, budget, and schedule requirements. | [Supplemental] Coordinate the transportation of sets that are built off-site, and coordinate their setup at the site of use. | [Supplemental] Confer with conservators to determine how to handle an exhibit's environmental aspects, such as lighting, temperature, and humidity, so that objects will be protected and exhibits will be enhanced. | [Supplemental] Select and purchase lumber and hardware necessary for set construction. | [Supplemental] Arrange for outside contractors to construct exhibit structures. | [Supplemental] Incorporate security systems into exhibit layouts. | [Supplemental] Coordinate the removal of sets, props, and exhibits after productions or events are complete. | [Supplemental] Provide supportive materials for exhibits and displays, such as press kits, advertising, publicity notices, posters, brochures, catalogues, and invitations.

communicating, or controlling impulses. | [Core] Design music therapy experiences, using various musical elements to meet client's goals or objectives. | [Core] Sing or play musical instruments, such as keyboard, guitar, or percussion instruments. | [Core] Communicate with clients to build rapport, acknowledge their progress, or reflect upon their reactions to musical experiences. | [Core] disabilities, or wellness. | [Core] Establish client goals or objectives for music therapy treatment, considering client needs, capabilities, interests, overall therapeutic program, coordination of treatment, or length of treatment. | [Core] Document evaluations, treatment plans, case summaries, or progress or other reports related to individual clients or client groups. | [Core] Assess client functioning levels, strengths, and areas of need in terms of perceptual, sensory, affective, communicative, musical, physical, cognitive, social, spiritual, or other abilities. | [Core] Observe and document client reactions, progress, or other outcomes related to music therapy. | [Core] Improvise instrumentally, vocally, or physically to meet client's therapeutic needs. | [Core] Gather transitions, pacing, sequencing, energy level, or intensity in accordance with treatment plans. | [Core] Engage clients in music experiences to identify client responses to different styles of music, findings and recommendations in oral, written, audio, video, or other forms. | [Core] Integrate behavioral, developmental, improvisational, medical, or neurological approaches into music therapy treatments. | [Core] Confer with professionals on client's treatment team to develop, coordinate, or integrate treatment plans. | [Core] Select or adapt musical instruments, musical equipment, or non-musical materials, such as adaptive devices or visual aids, to meet treatment objectives. | [Core] Compose, arrange, or adapt music for music therapy treatments. | [Core] Identify and respond to emergency physical or mental health situations. | [Core] Analyze or synthesize client data to draw conclusions or make recommendations for therapy. | [Core] Collaborate with others to design or implement interdisciplinary treatment programs. | [Core] Conduct information sharing sessions, such as in-service workshops for other professionals, potential client groups, or the general community. | [Core] Apply selected research findings to practice. | [Core] Analyze data to determine the effectiveness of specific treatments or therapy approaches. | [Core] Supervise staff, volunteers, practicum students, or interns engaged in music therapy activities. | [Core] Assess the risks and benefits of treatment termination for clients. | [Core] Adapt existing or develop new music therapy assessment instruments or procedures to meet an individual client's needs. | [Core] Apply current technology to music therapy practices. | [Core] Conduct, or assist in the conduct of, music therapy research.

practice guidelines. | [Core] Provide patients with information needed to promote health, reduce risk factors, or prevent disease or disability. | [Core] Analyze and interpret patients' histories, symptoms, physical findings, or diagnostic information to develop appropriate diagnoses. | [Core] Diagnose or treat complex, unstable, comorbid, episodic, or emergency conditions in collaboration with other health care providers as necessary. | [Core] Prescribe medication dosages, routes, and frequencies, based on such patient characteristics as age and gender. | [Core] Diagnose or treat chronic health care problems, such as high blood pressure and diabetes. | [Core] Prescribe medications based on efficacy, safety, and cost as legally authorized. | [Core] Recommend diagnostic or therapeutic interventions with attention to safety, cost, invasiveness, simplicity, acceptability, adherence, and efficacy. | [Core] Detect and respond to adverse drug reactions, with special attention to vulnerable populations such as infants, children, pregnant and lactating women, or older adults. | [Core] Diagnose or treat acute health care problems, such as illnesses, infections, or injuries. | [Core] Counsel patients about drug regimens and possible side effects or interactions with other substances, such as food supplements, over-the-counter (OTC) medications, or herbal remedies. | [Core] Order, perform, or interpret the results of diagnostic tests, such as complete blood counts (CBCs), electrocardiograms (EKGs), and radiographs (x-rays). | [Core] Educate patients about self-management of acute or chronic illnesses, tailoring instructions to patients' individual circumstances. | [Core] Maintain current knowledge of state legal regulations for nurse practitioner practice, including reimbursement of services. | [Core] Recommend interventions to modify behavior associated with health risks. | [Core] Consult with, or refer patients to, appropriate specialists when conditions exceed the scope of practice or expertise. | [Core] Treat or refer patients for primary care conditions, such as headaches, hypertension, urinary tract infections, upper respiratory infections, and dermatological conditions. | [Core] Read current literature, talk with colleagues, or participate in professional organizations or conferences to keep abreast of developments in nursing. | [Core] Schedule follow-up visits to monitor patients or evaluate health or illness care. | [Core] Perform routine or annual physical examinations. | [Core] Maintain departmental policies and procedures in areas such as safety and infection control. | [Core] Advocate for accessible health care that minimizes environmental health risks. | [Core] Perform primary care procedures such as suturing, splinting, administering immunizations, taking cultures, and debriding wounds. | [Core] Provide patients or caregivers with assistance in locating health care resources. | [Core] Keep abreast of regulatory processes and payer systems, such as Medicare, Medicaid, managed care, and private sources. | [Core] Supervise or coordinate patient care or support staff activities.

tasks: [Core] Examine microscopic samples to identify diseases or other abnormalities. | [Core] Diagnose diseases or study medical conditions, using techniques such as gross pathology, histology, cytology, cytopathology, clinical chemistry, immunology, flow cytometry, or molecular biology. | [Core] Write pathology reports summarizing analyses, results, and conclusions. | [Core] Communicate pathologic findings to surgeons or other physicians. | [Core] Identify the etiology, pathogenesis, morphological change, and clinical significance of diseases. | [Core] Read current literature, talk with colleagues, or participate in professional organizations or conferences to keep abreast of developments in pathology. | [Core] Consult with physicians about ordering and interpreting tests or providing treatments. | [Core] Analyze and interpret results from tests, such as microbial or parasite tests, urine analyses, hormonal assays, fine needle aspirations (FNAs), and polymerase chain reactions (PCRs). | [Core] Review cases by analyzing autopsies, laboratory findings, or case investigation reports. | [Core] Manage medical laboratories. | [Core] Develop or adopt new tests or instruments to improve diagnosis of diseases. | [Core] Educate physicians, students, and other personnel in medical laboratory professions, such as medical technology, cytotechnology, or histotechnology. | [Core] Plan and supervise the work of the pathology staff, residents, or visiting pathologists. | [Core] Perform autopsies to determine causes of deaths. | [Supplemental] Diagnose infections, such as Hepatitis B and Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndrome (AIDS), by conducting tests to detect the antibodies that patients' immune systems make to fight such infections. | [Supplemental] Obtain specimens by performing procedures, such as biopsies or fine needle aspirations (FNAs) of superficial nodules. | [Supplemental] Conduct genetic analyses of deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) or chromosomes to diagnose small biopsies and cell samples. | [Supplemental] Conduct research and present scientific findings. | [Supplemental] Testify in depositions or trials as an expert witness.

tomography (CT), positron emission tomography (PET), nuclear cardiology treadmill studies, mammography, or ultrasound. | [Core] Document the performance, interpretation, or outcomes of all procedures medical professionals regarding image-based diagnoses. | [Core] Recognize or treat complications during and after procedures, including blood pressure problems, pain, oversedation, or bleeding. | treatments. | [Core] Establish or enforce standards for protection of patients or personnel. | [Core] Coordinate radiological services with other medical activities. | [Core] Instruct radiologic staff [Supplemental] Advise other physicians of the clinical indications, limitations, assessments, or risks of diagnostic and therapeutic applications of radioactive materials. | [Supplemental] Calculate, measure, or prepare radioisotope dosages. | [Supplemental] Check and approve the quality of diagnostic images before patients are discharged. | [Supplemental] Compare nuclear medicine procedures with other types of procedures, such as computed tomography, ultrasonography, nuclear magnetic resonance imaging, and angiography. | [Supplemental] Direct nuclear medicine technologists or technicians regarding desired dosages, techniques, positions, and projections. | [Supplemental] Establish and enforce radiation protection standards for patients and staff. | [Supplemental] Formulate plans and procedures for nuclear medicine departments. | [Supplemental] Monitor handling of radioactive materials to ensure that established procedures are followed. | [Supplemental] Prescribe radionuclides and dosages to be administered to individual patients. | [Supplemental] Review procedure requests and patients' medical histories to determine applicability of procedures and radioisotopes to be used. | [Supplemental] Teach nuclear medicine, diagnostic radiology, or other specialties at graduate educational level. | [Supplemental] Test dosage evaluation instruments and survey meters to ensure they are operating properly.

tasks: [Core] Maintain a proper sterile field during surgical procedures. | [Core] Count sponges, needles, and instruments before and after operation. | [Core] Hand instruments and supplies to surgeons and surgeons' assistants, hold retractors and cut sutures, and perform other tasks as directed by surgeon during operation. | [Core] Scrub arms and hands and assist the surgical team to scrub and put on gloves, masks, and surgical clothing. | [Core] Wash and sterilize equipment, using germicides and sterilizers. | [Core] Prepare patients for surgery, including positioning patients on the operating table and covering them with sterile surgical drapes to prevent exposure. | [Core] Prepare, care for, and dispose of tissue specimens taken for laboratory analysis. | [Core] Monitor and continually assess operating room conditions, including patient and surgical team needs. | [Core] Prepare dressings or bandages and apply or assist with their application following surgery. | [Core] Clean and restock operating room, gathering and placing equipment and supplies and arranging instruments according to instructions, such as a preference card. | [Core] Provide technical assistance to surgeons, surgical nurses, or anesthesiologists. | [Core] Operate, assemble, adjust, or monitor sterilizers, lights, suction machines, or diagnostic equipment to ensure proper operation. | [Core] Maintain supply of fluids, such as plasma, saline, blood, or glucose, for use during operations. | [Supplemental] Schedule surgical procedures for patients. | [Supplemental] Order surgical supplies. | [Supplemental] Maintain files and records of surgical procedures. | [Supplemental] Observe patients' vital signs to assess physical condition. | [Supplemental] Transport patients to and from the operating room.

the use of orthopedic braces, prostheses, or supportive devices. | [Core] Monitor operation of equipment and record use of equipment and administration of treatment. | [Core] Assist patients to dress, undress, or put on and remove supportive devices, such as braces, splints, or slings. | [Core] Attend or conduct continuing education courses, seminars, or in-service activities. | [Core] Fit patients therapeutic wound care.

tasks: [Core] Rescue survivors from burning buildings, accident sites, and water hazards. | [Core] Administer first aid and cardiopulmonary resuscitation to injured persons or provide emergency medical care such as basic or advanced life support. | [Core] Dress with equipment such as fire-resistant clothing and breathing apparatus. | [Core] Move toward the source of a fire, using knowledge of types of fires, construction design, building materials, and physical layout of properties. | [Core] Drive and operate fire fighting vehicles and equipment. | [Core] Respond to fire alarms and other calls for assistance, such as automobile and industrial accidents. | [Core] Search to locate fire survivors. | [Core] Operate pumps connected to high-pressure hoses. | [Core] Maintain contact with fire dispatchers at all times to notify them of the need for additional firefighters and supplies, or to detail any difficulties encountered. | [Core] Extinguish flames and embers to suppress fires, using shovels or engine- or hand-driven water or chemical pumps. | [Core] Maintain knowledge of current firefighting practices by participating in drills and by attending seminars, conventions, and conferences. | [Core] Select and attach hose nozzles, depending on fire type, and direct streams of water or chemicals onto fires. | [Core] Collaborate with other firefighters as a member of a firefighting crew. | [Core] Train new employees to control and suppress fires. | [Core] Position and climb ladders to gain access to upper levels of buildings, or to rescue individuals from burning structures. | [Core] Create openings in buildings for ventilation or entrance, using axes, chisels, crowbars, electric saws, or core cutters. | [Core] Participate in fire drills and demonstrations of fire fighting techniques. | [Core] Assess fires and situations and report conditions to superiors to receive instructions, using two-way radios. | [Core] Inspect fire sites after flames have been extinguished to ensure that there is no further danger. | [Core] Patrol burned areas after fires to locate and eliminate hot spots that may restart fires. | [Core] Take action to contain any hazardous chemicals that could catch fire, leak, or spill. | [Core] Prepare written reports that detail specifics of fire incidents. | [Core] Protect property from water and smoke, using waterproof salvage covers, smoke ejectors, and deodorants. | [Core] Inspect buildings for fire hazards and compliance with fire prevention ordinances, testing and checking smoke alarms and fire suppression equipment as necessary. | [Core] Collaborate with police to respond to accidents, disasters, and arson investigation calls. | [Core] Salvage property by removing broken glass, pumping out water, and ventilating buildings to remove smoke. | [Core] Clean and maintain fire stations and fire fighting equipment and apparatus. | [Core] Inform and educate the public on fire prevention. | [Core] Participate in physical training activities to maintain a high level of physical fitness. | [Supplemental] Orient self in relation to fire, using compass and map, and collect supplies and equipment dropped by parachute.

alarms. | [Core] Package collected pieces of evidence in securely closed containers, such as bags, crates, or boxes, to protect them. | [Core] Conduct inspections and acceptance testing of newly installed fire protection systems. | [Core] Analyze evidence and other information to determine probable cause of fire or explosion. | [Core] Photograph damage and evidence related to causes of fires problems, and inadequate or non-functional fire exits. | [Core] Examine fire sites and collect evidence such as glass, metal fragments, charred wood, and accelerant residue for use in determining the cause of a fire. | [Core] Instruct children about the dangers of fire. | [Core] Conduct fire code compliance follow-ups to ensure that corrective actions have been taken in cases where violations were found. | [Core] Inspect properties that store, handle, and use hazardous materials to ensure compliance with laws, codes, and regulations, and issue hazardous materials permits to facilities found in compliance. | [Core] Write detailed reports of fire inspections performed, fire code violations observed, and corrective recommendations offered. | [Core] Identify corrective actions necessary to bring properties into compliance with applicable fire codes, laws, regulations, and standards, and explain these measures to property owners or their representatives. | [Core] Develop or review fire exit plans. | [Core] Inspect and test fire protection or fire detection systems to verify that such systems are installed in accordance with appropriate laws, codes, ordinances, regulations, and standards. | [Core] Coordinate efforts with other organizations, such as law enforcement agencies. | [Core] Attend training classes to maintain current knowledge of fire prevention, safety, and firefighting procedures. | [Core] Review blueprints and plans for new or remodeled buildings to ensure the structures meet fire safety codes. | [Core] Teach fire investigation techniques to other firefighter personnel. | [Core] Conduct fire exit drills to monitor and evaluate evacuation procedures. | [Core] Teach public education programs on fire safety and prevention. | [Core] Recommend changes to fire prevention, inspection, and fire code endorsement procedures. | [Supplemental] Subpoena and interview witnesses, property owners, and building occupants to obtain information and sworn testimony. | [Supplemental] Conduct internal investigation to determine negligence and violation of laws and regulations by fire department employees. | [Supplemental] Test sites and materials to establish facts, such as burn patterns and flash points of materials, using test equipment. | [Supplemental] Dust evidence or portions of fire scenes for latent fingerprints. | [Supplemental] Arrange for the replacement of defective fire fighting equipment and for repair of fire alarm and sprinkler systems, making minor repairs such as servicing fire extinguishers when feasible. | [Supplemental] Issue permits for public assemblies. | [Supplemental] Supervise staff, training them, planning their work, and evaluating their performance. | [Supplemental] Develop and coordinate fire prevention programs, such as false alarm billing, fire inspection reporting, and hazardous materials management.

responsibilities, and work stations to employees in accordance with work requirements. | [Core] Present bills and accept payments. | [Core] Perform various financial activities, such as cash handling, of patients, plan special menus, supervise the assembly of regular and special diet trays, and oversee the delivery of food trolleys to hospital patients. | [Supplemental] Record production, operational, and personnel data on specified forms. | [Supplemental] Perform personnel actions, such as hiring and firing staff, providing employee orientation and training, and conducting supervisory activities, such as creating work schedules or organizing employee time sheets. | [Supplemental] Estimate ingredients and supplies required to prepare a recipe. | [Supplemental] Purchase or requisition supplies and equipment needed to ensure quality and timely delivery of services. | [Supplemental] Perform food preparation and serving duties, such as carving meat, preparing flambe dishes, or serving wine and liquor. | [Supplemental] Schedule parties and take reservations. | [Supplemental] Develop departmental objectives, budgets, policies, procedures, and strategies. | for repairs.

games. | [Core] Monitor payment of hand-delivered jackpots to ensure promptness. | [Core] Explain and interpret house rules, such as game rules or betting limits, for patrons. | [Core] Establish and of malfunctioning machines and document malfunctions needing repair. | [Core] Monitor patrons for signs of compulsive gambling, offering assistance if necessary. | [Core] Supervise the distribution of complimentary meals, hotel rooms, discounts, or other items given to players, based on length of play and amount bet. | [Core] Report customer-related incidents occurring in gaming areas to supervisors. | [Core] Attach "out of order" signs to malfunctioning machines, and notify technicians when machines need to be repaired or removed. | [Core] Enforce safety rules, and report or remove safety hazards as well as guests who are underage, intoxicated, disruptive, or cheating. | [Core] Exchange currency for customers, converting currency into requested combinations of bills and coins. | maintain slot machines and surrounding areas. | [Supplemental] Monitor functioning of slot machine coin dispensers and fill coin hoppers when necessary. | [Supplemental] Record, issue receipts for, and pay off bets. | [Supplemental] Determine how many gaming tables to open each day and schedule staff accordingly. | [Supplemental] Direct workers compiling summary sheets for each race or event to record amounts wagered and amounts to be paid to winners. | [Supplemental] Establish policies on types of gambling offered, odds, or extension of credit. | [Supplemental] Review operational expenses, budget estimates, betting accounts, or collection reports for accuracy. | [Supplemental] Interview and hire workers. | [Supplemental] Train, supervise, schedule, and evaluate workers.

regulations. | [Supplemental] Perform contract administration duties, assisting with bid openings or the awarding of contracts. | [Supplemental] Perform record checks on past or current licensees, as tasks: [Core] Document quantity, quality, type, weight, test result data, and value of materials or products to maintain shipping, receiving, and production records and files. | [Core] Weigh or measure materials, equipment, or products to maintain relevant records, using volume meters, scales, rules, or calipers. | [Core] Collect or prepare measurement, weight, or identification labels and attach them to products. | [Core] Examine products or materials, parts, subassemblies, and packaging for damage, defects, or shortages, using specification sheets, gauges, and standards charts. | [Core] Signal or instruct other workers to weigh, move, or check products. | [Core] Collect product samples and prepare them for laboratory analysis or testing. | [Core] Maintain, monitor, and clean work areas, such as recycling collection sites, drop boxes, counters and windows, and areas around scale houses. | [Supplemental] Compare product labels, tags, or tickets, shipping manifests, purchase orders, and bills of lading to verify accuracy of shipment contents, quality specifications, or weights. | [Supplemental] Remove from stock products or loads not meeting quality standards, and notify supervisors or appropriate departments of discrepancies or shortages. | [Supplemental] Inspect products and examination records to determine the number of defects per worker and the reasons for examiners' rejections. | [Supplemental] Store samples of finished products in labeled cartons and record their location. | [Supplemental] Count or estimate quantities of materials, parts, or products received or shipped. | [Supplemental] Communicate with customers and vendors to exchange information regarding products, materials, and services. | [Supplemental] Fill orders for products and samples, following order tickets, and forward or mail items. | [Supplemental] Operate scalehouse computers to obtain weight information about incoming shipments such as those from waste haulers. | [Supplemental] Sort products or materials into predetermined sequences or groupings for display, packing, shipping, or storage. | [Supplemental] Transport materials, products, or samples to processing, shipping, or storage areas, manually or using conveyors, pumps, or hand trucks. | [Supplemental] Unload or unpack incoming shipments.

tasks: [Core] Measure designated amounts of ingredients for terrazzo or grout, according to standard formulas and specifications, using graduated containers and scales, and load ingredients into portable mixer. | [Core] Grind surfaces with a power grinder, or polish surfaces with polishing or surfacing machines. | [Core] Cut metal division strips and press them into the terrazzo base for joints or changes of color to form designs or patterns or to help prevent cracks. | [Core] Blend marble chip mixtures, place into panels, and push a roller over the surface to embed the chips. | [Core] Modify mixing, grouting, grinding, or cleaning procedures, according to type of installation or material used. | [Core] Spread, level, or smooth concrete or terrazzo mixtures to form bases or finished surfaces, using rakes, shovels, hand or power trowels, hand or power screeds, or floats. | [Core] Grind curved surfaces or areas inaccessible to surfacing machine, such as stairways or cabinet tops, with portable hand grinder. | [Core] Wash polished terrazzo surface, using cleaner and water, and apply sealer and curing agent according to manufacturer's specifications, using brush or sprayer. | [Core] Position and secure moisture membrane and wire mesh in preparation for pouring base materials for terrazzo installation. | [Core] Fill slight grinding depressions with matching grout material and hand-trowel for a smooth, uniform surface. | [Core] Clean installation site, mixing and storage areas, tools, machines, and equipment, and store materials and equipment. | [Core] Sprinkle colored marble or stone chips, powdered steel, or coloring powder over surface to produce prescribed finish. | [Core] Wet surface to prepare for bonding, fill holes and cracks with grout or slurry, and smooth with a trowel. | [Core] Mix cement, sand, and water to produce concrete, grout, or slurry, using hoe, trowel, tamper, scraper, or concrete-mixing machine. | [Core] Chip, scrape, or grind high spots, ridges, or rough projections to finish concrete, using pneumatic chisel, hand chisel, or other hand tools. | [Core] Mold expansion joints and edges, using edging tools, jointers, or straightedges. | [Core] Move terrazzo installation materials, tools, machines, or work devices to work areas, manually or using wheelbarrow. | [Core] Clean chipped area, using wire brush, and feel and observe surface to determine if it is rough or uneven. | [Supplemental] Repair concrete by cutting out damaged areas, drilling holes for reinforcing rods, and positioning reinforcing rods, using power saw and drill. | [Supplemental] Precast terrazzo blocks in wooden forms. | [Supplemental] Wet concrete surface and rub with stone to smooth surface and obtain specified finish. | [Supplemental] Build wooden molds, clamping molds around areas to be repaired, or setting up frames to the proper depth and alignment. | [Supplemental] Spread roofing paper on surface of foundation and spread concrete onto roofing paper with trowel to form terrazzo base. | [Supplemental] Produce rough concrete surface, using broom. | [Supplemental] Remove frames when the foundation is dry. | [Supplemental] Signal truck driver to position truck to facilitate pouring concrete and move chute to direct concrete on forms.

to regulate pressure of tools at bottoms of boreholes. | [Core] Maintain records of footage drilled, location and nature of strata penetrated, materials and tools used, services rendered, and time sites. | [Supplemental] Position and prepare truck-mounted derricks at drilling areas specified on field maps. | [Supplemental] Lower and explode charges in boreholes to start flow of oil from wells.

connections to change circuit layouts, following work orders or diagrams. | [Core] Diagnose and correct problems from remote locations, using special switchboards to find the sources of problems. | bases, using telephones or two-way radios to receive instructions or technical advice, or to report equipment status. | [Core] Remove loose wires and other debris after work is completed. | [Core] manuals to obtain maintenance instructions pertaining to specific malfunctions. | [Core] Analyze test readings, computer printouts, and trouble reports to determine equipment repair needs and required repair methods. | [Core] Measure distances from landmarks to identify exact installation sites for equipment. | [Core] Enter codes needed to correct electronic switching system programming. | [Core] requested features, such as time-correlated call routing. | [Core] Dig holes or trenches as necessary for equipment installation and access. | [Core] Perform routine maintenance on equipment, including adjusting and lubricating components and painting worn or exposed areas. | [Supplemental] Clean switches and replace contact points, using vacuum hoses, solvents, and hand tools. | [Supplemental] Perform database verifications, using computers. | [Supplemental] Program computerized switches and switchboards to provide requested features. | [Supplemental] Provide input into the design and manufacturing of new equipment. | [Supplemental] Address special issues or situations, such as illegal or unauthorized use of equipment, or cases of electrical or acoustic shock. | [Supplemental] Install telephone station equipment, such as intercommunication systems, transmitters, receivers, relays, and ringers, and related apparatus, such as coin collectors, telephone booths, and switching-key equipment. | [Supplemental] Place intercept circuits on terminals to handle vacant lines in central office installations.

tasks: [Core] Check and maintain diving equipment, such as helmets, masks, air tanks, harnesses, or gauges. | [Core] Take appropriate safety precautions, such as monitoring dive lengths and depths and registering with authorities before diving expeditions begin. | [Core] Communicate with workers on the surface while underwater, using signal lines or telephones. | [Core] Descend into water with the aid of diver helpers, using scuba gear or diving suits. | [Core] Inspect and test docks, ships, buoyage systems, plant intakes or outflows, or underwater pipelines, cables, or sewers, using closed circuit television, still photography, and testing equipment. | [Core] Obtain information about diving tasks and environmental conditions. | [Core] Inspect the condition of underwater steel or wood structures. | [Core] Operate underwater video, sonar, recording, or related equipment to investigate underwater structures or marine life. | [Core] Repair ships, bridge foundations, or other structures below the water line, using caulk, bolts, and hand tools. | [Core] Cut and weld steel, using underwater welding equipment, jigs, and supports. | [Core] Carry out non-destructive testing, such as tests for cracks on the legs of oil rigs at sea. | [Core] Take test samples or photographs to assess the condition of vessels or structures. | [Core] Supervise or train other divers, including hobby divers. | [Core] Perform activities related to underwater search and rescue, salvage, recovery, or cleanup operations. | [Core] Recover objects by placing rigging around sunken objects, hooking rigging to crane lines, and operating winches, derricks, or cranes to raise objects. | [Core] Install, inspect, clean, or repair piping or valves. | [Core] Set or guide placement of pilings or sandbags to provide support for structures, such as docks, bridges, cofferdams, or platforms. | [Core] Install pilings or footings for piers or bridges. | [Core] Salvage wrecked ships or their cargo, using pneumatic power velocity and hydraulic tools and explosive charges, when necessary. | [Core] Remove obstructions from strainers or marine railway or launching ways, using pneumatic or power hand tools. | [Supplemental] Drill holes in rock and rig explosives for underwater demolitions. | [Supplemental] Remove rubbish or pollution from the sea. | [Supplemental] Perform offshore oil or gas exploration or extraction duties, such as conducting underwater surveys or repairing and maintaining drilling rigs or platforms. | [Supplemental] Cultivate or harvest marine species or perform routine work on fish farms.

systems to mitigate corrosion of geothermal plant equipment or structures. | [Supplemental] Backfill piping trenches to protect pipes from damage. | [Supplemental] Operate equipment, such as excavators, backhoes, rock hammers, trench compactors, pavement saws, grout mixers or pumps, geothermal loop reels, and coil tubing units (CTU).

tasks: [Core] Release air bubbles and smooth seams, using rollers. | [Core] Spray chopped fiberglass, resins, and catalysts onto prepared molds or dies using pneumatic spray guns with chopper attachments. | [Core] Mix catalysts into resins, and saturate cloth and mats with mixtures, using brushes. | [Core] Check completed products for conformance to specifications and for defects by measuring with rulers or micrometers, by checking them visually, or by tapping them to detect bubbles or dead spots. | [Core] Pat or press layers of saturated mat or cloth into place on molds, using brushes or hands, and smooth out wrinkles and air bubbles with hands or squeegees. | [Core] Select precut fiberglass mats, cloth, and wood-bracing materials as required by projects being assembled. | [Core] Bond wood reinforcing strips to decks and cabin structures of watercraft, using resin-saturated fiberglass. | [Core] Trim excess materials from molds, using hand shears or trimming knives. | [Supplemental] Apply layers of plastic resin to mold surfaces prior to placement of fiberglass mats, repeating layers until products have the desired thicknesses and plastics have jelled. | [Supplemental] Inspect, clean, and assemble molds before beginning work. | [Supplemental] Cure materials by letting them set at room temperature, placing them under heat lamps, or baking them in ovens. | [Supplemental] Apply lacquers and waxes to mold surfaces to facilitate assembly and removal of laminated parts. | [Supplemental] Repair or modify damaged or defective glass-fiber parts, checking thicknesses, densities, and contours to ensure a close fit after repair. | [Supplemental] Mask off mold areas not to be laminated, using cellophane, wax paper, masking tape, or special sprays containing mold-release substances. | [Supplemental] Check all dies, templates, and cutout patterns to be used in the manufacturing process to ensure that they conform to dimensional data, photographs, blueprints, samples, or customer specifications. | [Supplemental] Trim cured materials by sawing them with diamond-impregnated cutoff wheels.

operation of automatic machines to ensure that products meet specifications and to detect jams or malfunctions, making adjustments as necessary. | [Core] Set up, operate, or tend metal or plastic secure stock material or workpieces against stops, on arbors, or in chucks, fixtures, or automatic feeding mechanisms, manually or using hoists. | [Core] Read blueprints or job orders to determine oiling or cleaning machines, dies, or workpieces, or adding coolant to machine reservoirs. | [Core] Make minor electrical and mechanical repairs and adjustments to machines and notify supervisors when major service is required. | [Core] Compute data, such as gear dimensions or machine settings, applying knowledge of shop mathematics. | [Core] Start machines and turn handwheels or valves to engage programs for computer numerical control (CNC) machines to cut metal and plastic materials. | [Supplemental] Align layout marks with dies or blades.

vises. | [Core] Connect and turn regulator valves to activate and adjust gas flow and pressure so that desired flames are obtained. | [Core] Position and secure workpieces, using hoists, cranes, wire, be joined to ensure snug fit, using power grinders and hand tools. | [Core] Weld separately or in combination, using aluminum, stainless steel, cast iron, and other alloys. | [Core] Chip or grind off excess weld, slag, or spatter, using hand scrapers or power chippers, portable grinders, or arc-cutting equipment. | [Core] Develop templates and models for welding projects, using mathematical plan layout, assembly, and operations.

tasks: [Core] Examine stitched, collated, bound, or unbound product samples for defects, such as imperfect bindings, ink spots, torn pages, loose pages, or loose or uncut threads. | [Core] Read work orders to determine instructions and specifications for machine set-up. | [Core] Install or adjust bindery machine devices, such as knives, guides, rollers, rounding forms, creasing rams, or clamps, to accommodate sheets, signatures, or books of specified sizes. | [Core] Trim edges of books to size, using cutting machines, book trimming machines, or hand cutters. | [Core] Stitch or glue endpapers, bindings, backings, or signatures, using sewing machines, glue machines, or glue and brushes. | [Core] Monitor machine operations to detect malfunctions or to determine whether adjustments are needed. | [Core] Maintain records, such as daily production records, using specified forms. | [Core] Lubricate, clean, or make minor repairs to machine parts to keep machines in working condition. | [Core] Set up or operate bindery machines, such as coil binders, thermal or tape binders, plastic comb binders, or specialty binders. | [Core] Set up or operate machines that perform binding operations, such as pressing, folding, or trimming. | [Core] Prepare finished books for shipping by wrapping or packing books and stacking boxes on pallets. | [Core] Set up or operate glue machines by filling glue reservoirs, turning switches to activate heating elements, or adjusting glue flow or conveyor speed. | [Core] Train workers to set up, operate, and use automatic bindery machines. | [Supplemental] Insert book bodies in devices that form back edges of books into convex shapes and produce grooves that facilitate cover attachment. | [Supplemental] Cut cover material to specified dimensions, fitting and gluing material to binder boards by hand or machine. | [Supplemental] Cut binder boards to specified dimensions, using board shears, hand cutters, or cutting machines. | [Supplemental] Bind new books, using hand tools such as bone folders, knives, hammers, or brass binding tools. | [Supplemental] Perform highly skilled hand finishing binding operations, such as grooving or lettering. | [Supplemental] Imprint or emboss lettering, designs, or numbers on book covers, using gold, silver, or colored foil, and stamping machines. | [Supplemental] Compress sewed or glued signatures, using hand presses or smashing machines. | [Supplemental] Meet with clients, printers, or designers to discuss job requirements or binding plans. | [Supplemental] Form book bodies by folding and sewing printed sheets to form signatures and assembling signatures in numerical order. | [Supplemental] Design original or special bindings for limited editions or other custom binding projects. | [Supplemental] Punch holes in and fasten paper sheets, signatures, or other material, using hand or machine punches and staplers. | [Supplemental] Repair, restore, or rebind old, rare, or damaged books, using hand tools.

washers or dry-cleaning machines, or direct other workers to perform loading. | [Core] Sort and count articles removed from dryers, and fold, wrap, or hang them. | [Core] Start washers, dry cleaners, sources of stains, to locate color imperfections, and to identify items requiring special treatment. | [Supplemental] Apply chemicals to neutralize the effects of solvents. | [Supplemental] Receive and mark articles for laundry or dry cleaning with identifying code numbers or names, using hand or machine markers. | [Supplemental] Apply bleaching powders to spots and spray them with steam to remove stains from fabrics that do not respond to other cleaning solvents. | [Supplemental] Operate machines that comb, dry and polish furs, clean, sterilize and fluff feathers and blankets, or roll and package towels. | [Supplemental] Pre-soak, sterilize, scrub, spot-clean, and dry contaminated or stained articles, using neutralizer solutions and portable machines. | [Supplemental] Mix and add detergents, dyes, bleaches, starches, and other solutions and chemicals to clean, color, dry, or stiffen articles. | [Supplemental] Wash, dry-clean, or glaze delicate articles or fur garment linings by hand, using mild detergents or dry cleaning solutions. | [Supplemental] Match sample colors, applying knowledge of bleaching agent and dye properties, and types, construction, conditions, and colors of articles. | [Supplemental] Operate dry-cleaning machines to clean soiled articles. | [Supplemental] Iron or press articles, fabrics, and furs, using hand irons or pressing machines. | [Supplemental] Hang curtains, drapes, blankets, pants, and other garments on stretch frames to dry. | [Supplemental] Spray steam, water, or air over spots to flush out chemicals, dry material, raise naps, or brighten colors. | [Supplemental] Mend and sew articles, using hand stitching, adhesive patches, or sewing machines. | [Supplemental] Dye articles to change or restore their colors, using knowledge of textile compositions and the properties and effects of bleaches and dyes. | [Supplemental] Test fabrics in inconspicuous places to determine whether solvents will damage dyes or fabrics. | [Supplemental] Mix bleaching agents with hot water in vats, and soak material until it is bleached. | [Supplemental] Clean fabrics, using vacuums or air hoses. | [Supplemental] Start pumps to operate distilling systems that drain and reclaim dry cleaning solvents. | [Supplemental] Rinse articles in water and acetic acid solutions to remove excess dye and to fix colors. | [Supplemental] Immerse articles in bleaching baths to strip colors. | [Supplemental] Identify articles' fabrics and original dyes by sight and touch, or by testing samples with fire or chemical reagents. | [Supplemental] Spread soiled articles on work tables, and position stained portions over vacuum heads or on marble slabs.
