supervisors so that repairs can be scheduled. | [Core] Monitor process indicators, instruments, gauges, and meters to detect and report any possible problems. | [Core] Start pumps and open valves or use automated equipment to regulate the flow of oil in pipelines and into and out of tanks. | [Core] Operate control panels to coordinate and regulate process variables such as temperature and pressure, and to direct product flow rate, according to process schedules. | [Core] Verify that incoming and outgoing products are moving through the correct meters, and that meters are working properly. | [Core] Patrol units to monitor the amount of oil in storage tanks, and to verify that activities and operations are safe, efficient, and in compliance with regulations. | [Core] Plan movement of products through lines to processing, storage, and shipping units, using knowledge of system interconnections and capacities. | [Core] Control or operate manifold and pumping systems to circulate liquids through a petroleum refinery. | [Core] Operate auxiliary equipment and control multiple processing units during distilling or treating operations, moving controls that regulate valves, pumps, compressors, and auxiliary equipment. | [Core] Collect product samples by turning bleeder valves, or by lowering containers into tanks to obtain oil samples. | [Core] Read automatic gauges at specified intervals to determine the flow rate of oil into or from tanks, and the amount of oil in tanks. | [Core] Synchronize activities with other pumphouses to ensure a continuous flow of products and a minimum of contamination between products. | [Core] Record and compile operating data, instrument readings, documentation, and results of laboratory analyses. | [Core] Conduct general housekeeping of units, including wiping up oil spills and performing general cleaning duties. | [Core] Inspect pipelines, tightening connections and lubricating valves as necessary. | [Supplemental] | [Supplemental] Perform tests to check the qualities and grades of products, such as assessing levels of bottom sediment, water, and foreign materials in oil samples, using centrifugal testers. | [Supplemental] Calculate test result values, using standard formulas. | [Supplemental] Clean interiors of processing units by circulating chemicals and solvents within units. | [Supplemental] Clamp seals around valves to secure tanks. | [Supplemental] Coordinate shutdowns and major projects. | [Supplemental] Prepare calculations for receipts and deliveries of oil and oil products. | [Supplemental] Lower thermometers into tanks to obtain temperature readings.

tasks: [Core] Monitor equipment operation, gauges, and panel lights to detect deviations from standards. | [Core] Confer with supervisors or other equipment operators to report equipment malfunctions or to resolve production problems. | [Core] Press and adjust controls to activate, set, and regulate equipment according to specifications. | [Core] Record gauge readings, test results, and shift production in log books. | [Core] Read and interpret work orders and instructions to determine work assignments, process specifications, and production schedules. | [Core] Examine or test samples of processed substances, or collect samples for laboratory testing, to ensure conformance to specifications. | [Core] Transport materials and products to and from work areas, manually or using carts, handtrucks, or hoists. | [Supplemental] Stop equipment and clear blockages or jams, using fingers, wire, or hand tools. | [Supplemental] Load equipment receptacles or conveyors with material to be processed, by hand or using hoists. | [Supplemental] Remove products from equipment, manually or using hoists, and prepare them for storage, shipment, or additional processing. | [Supplemental] Calculate amounts of materials to be loaded into furnaces, adjusting amounts as necessary for specific conditions. | [Supplemental] Melt or refine metal before casting, calculating required temperatures, and observe metal color, adjusting controls as necessary to maintain required temperatures. | [Supplemental] Weigh or measure specified amounts of ingredients or materials for processing, using devices such as scales and calipers. | [Supplemental] Direct crane operators and crew members to load vessels with materials to be processed. | [Supplemental] Feed fuel, such as coal and coke, into fireboxes or onto conveyors, and remove ashes from furnaces, using shovels and buckets. | [Supplemental] Replace worn or defective equipment parts, using hand tools. | [Supplemental] Clean, lubricate, and adjust equipment, using scrapers, solvents, air hoses, oil, and hand tools.

tasks: [Core] Examine completed work to detect defects and verify conformance to work orders, and adjust machinery as necessary to correct production problems. | [Core] Observe operation of various machines to detect and correct machine malfunctions such as improper forming, glue flow, or pasteboard tension. | [Core] Start machines and move controls to regulate tension on pressure rolls, to synchronize speed of machine components, and to adjust temperatures of glue or paraffin. | [Core] Disassemble machines to maintain, repair, or replace broken or worn parts, using hand or power tools. | [Supplemental] Install attachments to machines for gluing, folding, printing, or cutting. | [Supplemental] Cut products to specified dimensions, using hand or power cutters. | [Supplemental] Place rolls of paper or cardboard on machine feed tracks, and thread paper through gluing, coating, and slitting rollers. | [Supplemental] Monitor finished cartons as they drop from forming machines into rotating hoppers and into gravity feed chutes to prevent jamming. | [Supplemental] Adjust guide assemblies, forming bars, and folding mechanisms according to specifications, using hand tools. | [Supplemental] Measure, space, and set saw blades, cutters, and perforators, according to product specifications. | [Supplemental] Fill glue and paraffin reservoirs, and position rollers to dispense glue onto paperboard. | [Supplemental] Stamp products with information such as dates, using hand stamps or automatic stamping devices. | [Supplemental] Remove finished cores, and stack or place them on conveyors for transfer to other work areas. | [Supplemental] Lift tote boxes of finished cartons, and dump cartons into feed hoppers.

tasks: [Core] Lift raw materials, finished products, and packed items, manually or using hoists. | [Core] Mark or tag identification on parts. | [Core] Observe equipment operations so that malfunctions can be detected, and notify operators of any malfunctions. | [Core] Count finished products to determine if product orders are complete. | [Core] Examine products to verify conformance to quality standards. | [Core] Operate machinery used in the production process, or assist machine operators. | [Core] Load and unload items from machines, conveyors, and conveyances. | [Core] Remove products, machine attachments, or waste material from machines. | [Core] Separate products according to weight, grade, size, or composition of materials used to produce them. | [Core] Pack and store materials and products. | [Core] Wash work areas, machines, equipment, vehicles, or products. | [Core] Place products in equipment or on work surfaces for further processing, inspecting, or wrapping. | [Core] Transfer finished products, raw materials, tools, or equipment between storage and work areas of plants and warehouses, by hand or using hand trucks or powered lift trucks. | [Core] Help production workers by performing duties of lesser skill, such as supplying or holding materials or tools, or cleaning work areas and equipment. | [Supplemental] Prepare raw materials for processing. | [Supplemental] Read gauges or charts, and record data obtained. | [Supplemental] Start machines or equipment to begin production processes. | [Supplemental] Record information, such as the number of products tested, meter readings, or dates and times of product production. | [Supplemental] Turn valves to regulate flow of liquids or air, to reverse machines, to start pumps, or to regulate equipment. | [Supplemental] Tie products in bundles for further processing or shipment, following prescribed procedures. | [Supplemental] Measure amounts of products, lengths of extruded articles, or weights of filled containers to ensure conformance to specifications. | [Supplemental] Signal coworkers to direct them to move products during the production process. | [Supplemental] Position spouts or chutes of storage bins so that containers can be filled. | [Supplemental] Attach slings, ropes, or cables to objects such as pipes, hoses, or bundles. | [Supplemental] Break up defective products for reprocessing. | [Supplemental] Perform minor repairs to machines, such as replacing damaged or worn parts. | [Supplemental] Fold products and product parts during processing. | [Supplemental] Cut or break flashing from materials or products. | [Supplemental] Change machine gears, using wrenches. | [Supplemental] Clean and lubricate equipment. | [Supplemental] Dump materials such as prepared ingredients into machine hoppers prior to mixing. | [Supplemental] Unclamp and hoist full reels from braiding, winding, or other fabricating machines, using power hoists. | [Supplemental] Mix ingredients according to specified procedures or formulas. | [Supplemental] Thread ends of items such as thread, cloth, and lace through needles and rollers, and around take-up tubes.

operating levels and to detect equipment malfunctions. | [Core] Observe packages moving along conveyors to identify packages, detect defective packaging, and perform quality control. | [Core] Position deflector bars, gates, chutes, or spouts to divert flow of materials from one conveyor onto another conveyor. | [Core] Clean, sterilize, and maintain equipment, machinery, and work stations, using hand tools, shovels, brooms, chemicals, hoses, and lubricants. | [Core] Record production data such as weights, types, quantities, and storage locations of materials, as well as equipment performance problems and downtime. | [Core] Inform supervisors of equipment malfunctions that need to be addressed. | [Supplemental] Manipulate controls, levers, and valves to start pumps, auxiliary equipment, or conveyors, and to adjust equipment positions, speeds, timing, and material flows. | [Supplemental] Distribute materials, supplies, and equipment to work stations, using lifts and trucks. | [Supplemental] Press console buttons to deflect packages to predetermined accumulators or reject lines. | [Supplemental] Thread strapping through strapping tools and secure battens with strapping to form protective pallets around extrusions. | [Supplemental] Operate elevator systems in conjunction with conveyor systems. | [Supplemental] Weigh or measure materials and products, using scales or other measuring instruments, or read scales on conveyors that continually weigh products, to verify specified tonnages and prevent overloads. | [Supplemental] Read production and delivery schedules, and confer with supervisors, to determine sorting and transfer procedures, arrangement of packages on pallets, and destinations of loaded pallets. | [Supplemental] Operate consoles to control automatic palletizing equipment. | [Supplemental] Contact workers in work stations or other departments to request movement of materials, products, or machinery, or to notify them of incoming shipments and their estimated delivery times. | [Supplemental] Affix identifying information to materials or products, using hand tools. | [Supplemental] Collect samples of materials or products, checking them to ensure conformance to specifications or sending them to laboratories for analysis. | [Supplemental] Move, assemble, and connect hoses or nozzles to material hoppers, storage tanks, conveyor sections or chutes, and pumps. | [Supplemental] Repair or replace equipment components or parts such as blades, rolls, and pumps. | [Supplemental] Measure dimensions of bundles, using rulers, and cut battens to required sizes, using power saws. | [Supplemental] Join sections of conveyor frames at temporary working areas, and connect power units.
